## Why

`--instance grok-bot` defaulted to `~/demo-gate` — the web-agent demo's instance — because that is the path `examples/grok-bot-connector/runbook.md` named. #488 handled the collision with a `demo-instance.json` marker that refuses a second demo in one directory, but a marker can only refuse *after* the operator has typed the wrong `--instance` at the wrong directory, and the recovery is a reset of something they did not mean to touch.

Three demos, three directories:

```
web-agent   ~/demo-gate
guest       ~/demo-guest
grok-bot    ~/demo-grok-bot
```

`--path <dir>` still puts any instance anywhere, and the marker stays as the backstop for exactly that case.

## What moved

- `examples/demo-provision.mjs`: the `grok-bot` default, the header table and the `--help` block.
- `examples/grok-bot-connector/runbook.md`: all 33 `demo-gate` references were that instance's path, including the clone target and the payload's `cwd`; none were the policy filename.
- `examples/README.md`: the Grok row, and the paragraph that explained the shared default now explains the marker as a backstop instead.
- `examples/web-agent-demo/provisioning.md`: the one comment naming the instance.

## Pinned

New test, `the three instances have three different default directories`, reads the defaults out of the `--help` block and asserts three distinct paths — a future shared default fails in CI rather than on a demo morning.

## Verification

`npm ci && npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm run lint` clean. `node scripts/run-tests.mjs --only demo-provision`: 17/17 (16 from #488 plus the new one). `--only demo-guest-limits --only docs-guard`: 20/20. The local SMTP/TLS suites still fail on this machine's Node v26 as they did before #488; CI on Node 22 is the truth.

Follow-up to #488, on APRV-386.
